details: Cryptocurrency-related stocks and major digital assets like Bitcoin and Ethereum surged after the U.S. Treasury Department announced plans to increase long-duration bond buybacks, a move that typically boosts risk assets. Further positive sentiment came from President Donald Trump's call for Congress to pass the "Clarity Act" to establish clearer regulatory rules for the digital asset sector. Additionally, analysts suggest that underlying support for Bitcoin's rally could stem from Federal Reserve liquidity promises and a perceived structural decline in the Dollar Index, which recently hit its lowest point since May. Bitcoin has reportedly climbed above $72,000, reaching its highest level since June.
title: Crypto Rallies on Treasury Bond Buybacks, Trump's Policy Push, and Dollar Weakness

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) has expressed significant concern that the current rapid growth in artificial intelligence investments might be unsustainable, potentially leading to a global stock market crash. ECB researchers drew historical parallels to past technological bubbles, suggesting that present market valuations in the AI sector resemble previous speculative peaks. They cautioned that the interconnectedness of global financial markets means any correction in the AI bubble could destabilize the broader worldwide economy.
title: ECB Warns AI Boom Could Spark Global Stock Market Crash

details: European Central Bank policymaker Olli Rehn stated on Wednesday that wage growth and the wage outlook in the Eurozone have remained moderate, with no clear evidence of "second-round effects" that could entrench inflation. Rehn emphasized the importance of keeping inflation expectations anchored, ahead of the ECB's upcoming monetary policy announcement.
title: ECB Policymaker Rehn Notes Moderate Wage Growth Amid Inflation Concerns

details: The cryptocurrency futures market recently experienced a "brutal washout," with over $603 million in cumulative liquidations, primarily affecting long positions. This significant sell-off was driven by cascading margin calls and exacerbated by high leverage, leading to a rapid drying up of market liquidity. Bitcoin saw an approximate 3% decline, while other altcoins experienced even sharper drops, highlighting the amplified impact of price changes in highly leveraged environments.
title: Cryptocurrency Futures Market Sees $603 Million in Liquidations
